_comment: Octail curated egg (plan §6.4). Based on games-steamcmd eco/egg-eco.json (pelican-eggs, MIT licence). Octail makes the Strange Loop Games account optional (--username/--password only when set; upstream required it), adds automatic web and RCON ports instead of empty required ones, the eco tag, install sandbox defaults and resource hints, and makes the install fail when SteamCMD didn't download the server. SteamCMD is retried up to 3 times: its first run on a fresh install often fails with "Missing configuration". Without an SLG account the server starts with -offline (it refuses to start with neither). Octail also wires up RCON (the existing RCON_PORT/RCON_PW already written into Network.eco) and the Players tab: Eco's own /manage commands are confirmed over the standard Source RCON wire protocol by hand against a live 0.14.2 beta server, including its console not supporting quotes at all and using a literal comma, not whitespace, as its real argument separator. Restart warnings use the Players tab's broadcast (/manage announce, over RCON; the panel's fallback for RCON games, say, is not an Eco command). kick/ban/unban are reliable; the player list (/manage players) is only confirmed empty ("Online:" with nobody on), the non-empty row format couldn't be observed with a real connected player, so tentacle/src/players/index.js ships a best-effort, low-confidence comma-split guess for it rather than a verified format.
name: Eco
author: eggs@goover.dev
description: Eco is an online world from Strange Loop Games where players must build civilization using resources from an ecosystem that can be damaged and destroyed. The world of Eco is an incredibly reactive one, and whatever any player does in the world affects the underlying ecosystem.

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# steamcmd Base Installation Script
#
# Server Files: /mnt/server
# Image to install with is 'ghcr.io/parkervcp/installers:debian'

##
#
# Variables
# STEAM_USER, STEAM_PASS, STEAM_AUTH - Steam user setup. If a user has 2fa enabled it will most likely fail due to timeout. Leave blank for anon install.
# WINDOWS_INSTALL - if it's a windows server you want to install set to 1
# SRCDS_APPID - steam app id found here - https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Dedicated_Servers_List
# SRCDS_BETAID - beta branch of a steam app. Leave blank to install normal branch
# SRCDS_BETAPASS - password for a beta branch should one be required during private or closed testing phases.. Leave blank for no password.
# INSTALL_FLAGS - Any additional SteamCMD  flags to pass during install.. Keep in mind that steamcmd auto update process in the docker image might overwrite or ignore these when it performs update on server boot.
# AUTO_UPDATE - Adding this variable to the egg allows disabling or enabling automated updates on boot. Boolean value. 0 to disable and 1 to enable.
#
 ##

# Install packages. Default packages below are not required if using our existing install image thus speeding up the install process.
#apt -y update
#apt -y --no-install-recommends install curl lib32gcc-s1 ca-certificates

## just in case someone removed the defaults.
if [[ "${STEAM_USER}" == "" ]] || [[ "${STEAM_PASS}" == "" ]]; then
    echo -e "steam user is not set.\n"
    echo -e "Using anonymous user.\n"
    STEAM_USER=anonymous
    STEAM_PASS=""
    STEAM_AUTH=""
else
    echo -e "user set to ${STEAM_USER}"
fi

## download and install steamcmd
cd /tmp
mkdir -p /mnt/server/steamcmd
curl -sSL -o steamcmd.tar.gz https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/client/installer/steamcmd_linux.tar.gz
tar -xzvf steamcmd.tar.gz -C /mnt/server/steamcmd
mkdir -p /mnt/server/steamapps # Fix steamcmd disk write error when this folder is missing
cd /mnt/server/steamcmd

# SteamCMD fails otherwise for some reason, even running as root.
# This is changed at the end of the install process anyways.
chown -R root:root /mnt
export HOME=/mnt/server

## install game using steamcmd
## Octail: SteamCMD's first run often fails with "Missing configuration"; try up to 3 times
for steamcmd_try in 1 2 3; do
    if ./steamcmd.sh +force_install_dir /mnt/server +login ${STEAM_USER} ${STEAM_PASS} ${STEAM_AUTH} $( [[ "${WINDOWS_INSTALL}" == "1" ]] && printf %s '+@sSteamCmdForcePlatformType windows' ) +app_update ${SRCDS_APPID} $( [[ -z ${SRCDS_BETAID} ]] || printf %s "-beta ${SRCDS_BETAID}" ) $( [[ -z ${SRCDS_BETAPASS} ]] || printf %s "-betapassword ${SRCDS_BETAPASS}" ) ${INSTALL_FLAGS} validate +quit; then break; fi
    echo "SteamCMD did not finish (attempt $steamcmd_try of 3)"
done

## set up 32 bit libraries
mkdir -p /mnt/server/.steam/sdk32
cp -v linux32/steamclient.so ../.steam/sdk32/steamclient.so

## set up 64 bit libraries
mkdir -p /mnt/server/.steam/sdk64
cp -v linux64/steamclient.so ../.steam/sdk64/steamclient.so

# add below your custom commands if needed

## Octail: fail the install when SteamCMD didn't download the server
if [[ ! -f "/mnt/server/EcoServer" ]]; then
    echo -e "\nSteamCMD failed to install the Eco dedicated server; try reinstalling."
    exit 1
fi
chmod +x /mnt/server/EcoServer

FILE=$HOME/Configs/Network.eco
if [ -f "$FILE" ]; then
  echo -e "Network.eco found."
else  
  echo -e "No Network.eco found. Moving default..."
  cp -f $HOME/Configs/Network.eco.template $HOME/Configs/Network.eco
  echo -e ".done.."
fi

FILE=$HOME/Configs/Localization.eco
if [ -f "$FILE" ]; then
  echo -e "Localization.eco found."
else  
  echo -e "No Localization.eco found. Moving default..."
  cp -f $HOME/Configs/Localization.eco.template $HOME/Configs/Localization.eco
  echo -e "..done.."
fi

echo "-----------------------------------------"
echo "Installation completed..."
echo "-----------------------------------------"

variables.name: [SERVER] Webserver Port
variables.description: The web server port (TCP): the web map, stats and API. Set by Octail when the server is created (the port after the game port).

variables.name: [SERVER] Public Server
variables.description: Set to True to have the server listed in the Eco client

variables.name: [SERVER] Server Password
variables.description: Set a password for the server, or leave this blank to not require a password. Players on the whitelist will not have to enter a password.

variables.name: [SERVER] Server Name
variables.description: Sets the name of your server in the client server browser. Chat_Commands#Text_markup can be used to add color or modify the appearance of the text.

variables.name: [SERVER] Max Connections
variables.description: Maximum number of concurrent players (-1 no limits).

variables.name: [SERVER] Playtime
variables.description: This is automatically filled in if you created the server in the Eco client and made a Timetable (schedule of preferred playtimes). If this is blank, the best way to fill it in is to “Set Playtime” through the Game Menu (Esc), and copy and paste the data from playtime.eco.

variables.name: [SERVER] Detailed Description
variables.description: Sets the long-form description of your server when people click on it in the server browser. Adding this description helps the server show up more prominently in the browser.

variables.name: [SERVER] RCON Port
variables.description: RCON port (TCP), written to Network.eco. Set by Octail when the server is created (two after the game port).

variables.name: [SERVER] Discord Server
variables.description: Invite link ID for a Discord server (the ID after the “discord.gg/”).

variables.name: [SERVER] Server Category
variables.description: Choose from 1 of 4 categories that will show up when players first click on “New Game” in the Eco client. Selecting a category makes it much more likely new players will join your server. Strings available for this option are: None; Beginner; Established; BeginnerHard; Strange

variables.name: [ACCOUNT] SLG Username
variables.description: Optional: a Strange Loop Games account name, passed with --username when set. Spaces are fine; quotes, backslashes, $ and ` are not.

variables.name: [ACCOUNT] SLG Password
variables.description: The password of that account (--password). Spaces are fine; quotes, backslashes, $ and ` are not.
